messages:
maria (sec): Heads-up — support reported a customer where a user with the Viewer role could update project settings via the console API path. They saw a successful PATCH on membership role. Can someone triage?
kevin (eng): ack. any repro data? token type?
maria (sec): customer used a machine token (legacy project token). repro attached by support: curl shows 200 when changing member role.
kevin (eng): curious, viewer should be blocked before hitting the project-member PATCH handler. quick repro from my end:
```
TOKEN=xxx_legacy_project_token
curl -i -X PATCH \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://console.redwood.example/api/v1/projects/123/members/456 \
  -d '{"role":"editor"}'
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n# {"updated":true}
```
maria (sec): that's the one. support attached audit event showing action succeeded but UI shows viewer.
olivia (product): is this purely an API auth-path bug or a role-mapping regression from the recent roles refactor? we shipped the matrix change last week.
kevin (eng): looks like a mapping mismatch between the console UI gating and the API permission evaluator. The legacy token path was short-circuited in the refactor and gets the old "project:owner" scope from the cached token blob.
jordan (devex): we also changed KMS alias name during rotation on friday — could decrypt failures have triggered fallback behavior? the audit logs show some KMS errors earlier.
audit-bot: log snippet: "2025-02-11T18:03:12Z audit: token_verify failed: kms:Decrypt failed for alias/redwood-project-2024 -> fallback to legacy-scope=true"
sre-ops: if fallback flips legacy-scope to true, that explains the elevated API permissions. this is high severity.
maria (sec): agree. customer impact: potential privilege escalation for any holder of legacy project tokens. need immediate mitigation steps.
kevin (eng): proposed immediate mitigations:
- disable minting/acceptance of legacy project tokens globally (fast rollback)
- bulk revoke tokens issued before 2025-02-01 and force re-issue with new scope
- hotfix to API gate: ensure explicit server-side role check on membership PATCH independent of token blob scope

jordan (devex): i can draft a user-facing blurb and CS playbook for token revocation + how to re-issue.
olivia (product): we should also prepare an incident postmortem if we roll this out. include timeline and affected orgs.
maria (sec): action owners:
- kevin: hotfix gate + deploy (ETA 2h)
- jordan: CS script + customer notifications (ETA 1h)
- sre-ops: run emergency KMS decrypt job to validate aliases and rotate back if needed (ETA 3h)
- maria: coordinate vulnerability advisory and legal notification if required

kevin (eng): quick checklist I'm following: add unit + e2e for API evaluator, add a failing test that uses legacy token blob, ensure KMS decrypt failures throw 401 not fallback, then canary deploy to staging.
maria (sec): also add audit telemetry for any membership write where requester role == viewer to alert on anomalies.
jordan (devex): customer playbook drafted: revoke, reissue token, check member list, confirm no unauthorized changes. ready to share with CS.
kevin (eng): patch landed to branch, running CI. will post CI link in 15m.
maria (sec): thanks. we'll reconvene after hotfix verification. tagging for followup: @kevin @jordan @sre-ops
kevin (eng): noted. pushing the fix now. :lock:
